- `bun test scripts/ packages/runtime/tests/version.test.ts` -> exit 0, 116 pass, 0 fail.
- `bunx --no-install mise run verify` -> exit 0. Check, lint and format are clean; the tests give 1125 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail.
- `/code-review` on `0f52c9d...5c98d8e` ran with the built-in skill. I classified its 7 findings below.

findings:
1. **Blocking.** `packages/integrations/claude/build.ts:40`: the sync runs too late.
   - `build.ts` statically imports `src/generate.ts`, which does `import packageJson from "../package.json"`. Bun evaluates that import before the `import.meta.main` body, so `generate.ts` has the old version cached before `syncVersions` rewrites the file.
   - Reproduced in the scratch copy: `bump-version.ts patch` then `bun build.ts` left `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `dist/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` at 0.2.1 while every other copy was 0.2.2. The copy-equality test then failed. A second build fixed it.
   - So `mise run bump:patch` or `bump:minor` ships stale manifests, which breaks the "build keeps every copy equal" requirement.
   - Smallest fix: make the sync its own step, `run = ["bun scripts/bump-version.ts sync", "bun packages/integrations/claude/build.ts"]` in the mise `build` task, and drop the call from `build.ts`. Alternatively, import `generate.ts` dynamically after the sync. Add a test that bumps and builds a temp tree once and checks the manifests.
2. Non-blocking. `scripts/bump-version.ts:128`: `WORKSPACE_VERSION` still matches only `\n`, so audit B7 (CRLF lockfile) is not fixed. `.gitattributes` has `* text=auto eol=lf`, so git checkouts are LF and the practical risk is low. Fix: use `\r?\n`.
3. Non-blocking. `scripts/bump-version.ts:~190`: `syncVersions` writes the copies one at a time, so a failure part-way leaves a half-synced tree. The sync is idempotent, so re-running it repairs the tree. Load every copy first, then write.
4. Non-blocking. `mise.toml:70-80`: the comment ("The script rewrites the package.json files and bun.lock") and the descriptions ("everywhere") are stale. Fix the wording.
5. Optional. `packages/runtime/src/cli/program.ts:6`: importing the whole root `package.json` embeds its `devDependencies`, scripts and the rest in `dist/scripts/holyagent.js`. Any later root-manifest change therefore alters the generated bundle. It works, but a build-time define of the version would avoid that.
6. Rejected.
   - `writeManifest` re-reading the source file: harmless.
   - The bundle-version test depending on a rebuilt dist: that is intended drift detection.
   - The sync living in the `import.meta.main` block: this duplicates finding 1.

Checked and fine:
- The root `package.json` is the only hand-edited copy.
- `bump` edits only the root file.
- `sync` is idempotent: a file already at the version is not written, and the lockfile is written only if its text changed.
- The copy test compares the root against two workspace manifests, the lockfile workspaces, `plugin.json` and `marketplace.json`, so a drifted copy fails it.
- `dist/scripts/holyagent.js` has the root manifest inlined and has no run-time read of `package.json`, so it does not depend on files outside the plugin. I confirmed this by reading the bundle, not by running it from an installed plugin.
- No try/catch, `new Promise` or async functions in the new code beyond `build.ts`, which was already async; the new code uses Effect and Schema.
